paper_metadata.title: Text2KGBench: A Benchmark for Ontology-Driven Knowledge Graph Generation from Text

evidence.excerpt: DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.7916716

paper_metadata.abstract: Text2KGBench is a benchmark for evaluating language models that generate knowledge-graph facts from natural-language sentences under ontology guidance. Given an ontology and sentences, systems must extract faithful facts while using the ontology's concepts, relations, and domain/range constraints. It provides Wikidata-TekGen (10 ontologies; 13,474 sentences) and DBpedia-WebNLG (19 ontologies; 4,860 sentences), seven metrics for extraction, ontology conformance, and hallucination, and Vicuna-13B and Alpaca-LoRA-13B prompted baselines.

problem_addressed: The paper addresses the lack of an evaluation benchmark for extracting sentence-grounded KG facts with an explicit ontology as input. It evaluates whether language models can select canonical ontology relations, extract facts faithful to a sentence rather than model pretraining knowledge, and avoid fabricated subjects, relations, or objects.

methodology.description: Text2KGBench specifies ontology-guided sentence-level fact extraction. For each case, a prompt combines: (1) a fixed instruction to output only triples, (2) a verbalized ontology listing concepts and canonical relations with domain/range signatures, (3) a similarity-selected training demonstration with its aligned triples, and (4) the test sentence. The decoder-only instruction-tuned LLM directly generates triples in relation(subject, object) notation. The benchmark parses these as output triples and evaluates exact fact extraction, use of ontology relations, and hallucinated subject/relation/object terms. The authors' baseline retrieves demonstrations using SBERT with T5-XXL sentence embeddings.

ontology_or_schema_use.value: Ontology is a required task input and prompt context. It specifies concepts, canonical relation names, and relation domain/range constraints. The current conformance metric checks whether the output relation name is in the ontology; the paper notes that validation could later extend to domain/range and other axioms. Ontologies are verbalized rather than supplied as direct RDF/OWL syntax.

input_output.input_type: A natural-language sentence, its associated ontology verbalization (concepts and relation signatures), a fixed extraction instruction, and one or more sentence-to-triple demonstrations from training data.
input_output.input_granularity: Sentence-level: each benchmark alignment pairs one natural-language sentence with one or more triples; baseline prompting processes each test sentence separately.
input_output.output_representation: A textual set of ontology-aligned triples written in relation(subject, object) notation. The benchmark treats the parsed text as LLM output triples; it does not evaluate direct RDF/OWL serialization in this version.

models_and_tools: Vicuna-13B baseline: LLaMA-13B with Vicuna/FastChat delta weights
Alpaca-LoRA-13B baseline: LLaMA base model adapted with Low-Rank Adaptation
Sentence Transformers (SBERT) with T5-XXL for nearest demonstration selection
scikit-learn for stratified randomized train/validation/test folds
Evaluation scripts that parse output triples and calculate seven metrics
datasets: Wikidata-TekGen: 10 manually formulated Wikidata-derived ontologies and 13,474 sentence–triple alignments; splits include all test cases, a manually cleaned/verified 939-alignment test subset, and 174 author-invented unseen sentences.
DBpedia-WebNLG: 19 ontologies derived from WebNLG categories and 4,860 sentence–triple alignments from WebNLG 3.0 English 3triples; train/test splitting prevents the same fact appearing in both.
Source corpora: TekGen (distantly supervised Wikidata triple–Wikipedia sentence alignments) and WebNLG 3.0 English.

metrics: Triple-level Precision (P): correct output triples divided by output triples
Triple-level Recall (R): correct output triples divided by gold triples
F1: harmonic mean of P and R
Ontology Conformance (OC): proportion of output triples whose relation is a canonical ontology relation
Subject Hallucination (SH): subject terms absent from the test sentence or ontology concepts, after stemming
Relation Hallucination (RH): relation absent from ontology relations, using exact matching
Object Hallucination (OH): object terms absent from the test sentence or ontology concepts, after stemming
baselines: Vicuna-13B with automatically generated ontology-guided in-context prompts
Alpaca-LoRA-13B with automatically generated ontology-guided in-context prompts
evaluation.setting: The authors run inference on automatically generated prompts over Wikidata-TekGen and DBpedia-WebNLG, aggregate results across 10 and 19 ontologies respectively, and report P/R/F1, OC, SH/RH/OH. Wikidata-TekGen is evaluated in All, Selected (manually validated), and Unseen variants. The evaluation uses exact comparison of generated and gold triples, but applies a locally closed approach that considers only relations appearing in the gold truth to reduce false negatives because sentence triple sets are non-exhaustive.

value: For Vicuna-13B on all Wikidata-TekGen cases, ontology-level F1 ranges from 0.24 (Military) to 0.66 (Space); OC ranges from 0.59 (Culture) to 0.94 (Music).

value: Author contribution: the benchmark operationalizes ontology-guided fact extraction with datasets, seven metrics, evaluation scripts, baseline prompts, responses, and results, covering extraction accuracy, canonical-relation conformance, and three hallucination types.

[Review inference] Separating cleaned and author-invented unseen Wikidata-TekGen test variants makes benchmark noise and possible pretraining-data exposure visible rather than relying only on distant-supervision alignments.
[Review inference] Providing ontology-specific results demonstrates that aggregate scores can conceal substantial variation by ontology (e.g., Vicuna all-test F1 from 0.24 to 0.66).

value: [Review inference] The benchmark's current OC metric validates only whether a relation name is canonical; therefore a high OC score does not establish that the output satisfies declared domain/range constraints or other ontology axioms.

[Review inference] The locally closed triple-matching protocol can under-penalize sentence-supported triples whose relations are absent from non-exhaustive gold annotations, so its precision/recall values are scoped to the supplied gold relation set.

[Review inference] Baseline accuracy is modest despite high ontology conformance: the reported F1 values are 0.22–0.38 while OC is 0.83–0.93, showing that canonical relation selection alone is insufficient for correct fact extraction.

[Review inference] The reported baselines are limited to two 13B open-source instruction-tuned models with prompt-based inference; results do not establish performance for fine-tuned systems, direct RDF/OWL processing, or commercial models.
